findings.reason: a node building §4 must know whether the caller resolves the paths and passes them or passes the lineage for `launch_plan` to resolve, and the two readings yield different call-site signatures and write scopes.
findings.text: §4 states both that `launch_plan` "gains the paths to hide" and that "the launch looks up the primary's ledger row by the lineage's `primary_run_id` ... and passes that row to `promotion_scope._primary_read_targets`", while `launch_plan` in `reckon/_backends.py` receives no project or ledger (its parameters are backend, prompt, worktree, manifest_path and fence inputs) and `_shadow_stream_contamination`, the lookup §4 points at, runs in the crew layer with the loaded ledger passed in — so the two sentences place the resolution in different layers and one of them requires a new ledger parameter on every caller plus a crew import into a low-level composer

response_events.reason: valid; deferred to the revision of s4 before its dispatch, since s4 follows s2 and s3; the fix is recorded as comment c-s4-resolution-layer on s4

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — in the changed units every code anchor resolves (`promotion_scope._primary_read_targets` at promotion_scope.py:1040, `_shadow_stream_contamination` at 1080, `ledger.shadow_primary_read` at ledger.py:2889, `runs.run_dir` at runs.py:81, `review.review_path` at review.py:1969, `pair_shadow_arms` at capabilities.py:984, `fence_argv` at _worker_fence.py:1143, `launch_plan` at _backends.py:2081 calling `fence_argv` at 2214), the three named launch callers all call `launch_plan` (dispatch.py:1902, dispatch_sessions.py:1135 and 1589, resumption.py:555), and the referenced plans `jev-learns-from-its-routes` and `a-worker-cannot-write-your-home` both exist.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §2, §3 and §4 each name a mutation that must make an assertion fail, and the scan widening carries its own negative control (a call reading only the shadow's own worktree and run home gets none).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the done-whens write to committed tests under `tests/` and a committed fixture; no gate log or artifact is placed on a session scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new symbols `primary_run_directory_read`, `primary_review_read` and `primary_worktree_read` name the read they detect, and the write paths and test filenames carry no plan, sprint or ticket identifiers.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §2's root cause matches its evidence (nova's row carries `shadow_contaminated: primary_changed_path_read` while `shadow_controlled: True`, and `pair_shadow_arms` does read only `lineage.configuration`), and the fixture claim is grounded (the retained stream's tool inputs do name the primary's run directory and a primary-changed path), but §4 names two different places for resolving the primary's paths, one of which `launch_plan` cannot reach.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 joins one control verdict to the existing contamination scan, §3 renames one worktree session, §4 composes one fence mask set.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` puts s4 on s2 and s3, and §4 both masks the path set §2's `_primary_read_targets` returns and shares `dispatch.py` with §3, so the declared edges match the mechanism.
